write.prompt: Some people think that primary school children should learn English only through songs and games, while others believe they should also be taught simple grammar rules from the start. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
write.taskVi: essay 200–250 từ trong 40 phút, đồng hồ đếm ngược hiện trên màn hình. Không có câu mở đầu gợi ý.
mustUse: ít nhất hai lần quy chiếu bằng this / these / such + danh từ, và người đọc luôn biết từ quy chiếu đang chỉ ý nào. The former / the latter đã luyện ở chặng 2, không bắt buộc trong bài có giờ
write.modelAfterSubmit:
There is an ongoing debate about how young children should be taught English. Some people believe that songs and games should be the main method, whereas others argue that grammar should be taught from the very beginning. In my opinion, games should come first, but simple patterns can be introduced gradually.

Supporters of a playful approach point out that young learners acquire language best when they are relaxed and having fun. Singing, acting out stories and playing picture-card games allow children to hear the same words many times without feeling bored. Such activities also help them lose their fear of speaking, which is often a problem for older students.

On the other hand, those who favour early grammar believe that clear rules help children speak accurately. Without them, some pupils may remember many words but be unable to build a sentence. This concern is reasonable, especially for shy children who feel lost in noisy games. However, formal grammar lessons are difficult for seven-year-olds, who cannot yet follow abstract explanations.

Overall, both views have merit, but the former suits young children better. Teachers can start with songs and games, then point out simple patterns as children grow older. This step-by-step approach lays the groundwork for more formal study at secondary school.
